items.title: Idrus Harun among 4 appointed as members of Judicial Appointments Commission
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appointed four people, including former Attorney General Tan Sri Idrus Harun, as members of the Judicial Appointments Commission for a two-year term, effective today. Also appointed are former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali; Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) law lecturer Prof Dr Hartini Saripan (for a second term); and former Sabah State Attorney General Datuk Mariati Robert. The Office of the Secretary of the Judicial Appointments Commission, in a statement today, said the appointments were made in accordance with subsection 5(1)(f) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009.

items.title: Northeast monsoon: Let us strive towards zero flood-related fatalities
items.summary: LETTERS: As we enter the Northeast Monsoon season, I wish to call on all relevant authorities, disaster management agencies and communities to make ZERO FLOOD-RELATED FATALITIES our collective target and commitment. We must strive to ensure zero drownings, zero preventable deaths and zero avoidable tragedies throughout this monsoon season. Preparedness must be proactive rather than reactive.

items.title: Tok Mat to lead Malaysia’s delegation to CHOGM 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan will lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2026) and related meetings in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, from November 1 to 4. In a statement, the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said CHOGM 2026, themed “Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth”, will bring together Heads of State/Government and Ministers from 56 Commonwealth Member States. Wisma Putra said Malaysia’s participation in CHOGM 2026 reaffirms the Government’s commitment to promoting the principles and values enshrined in the Commonwealth Charter and strengthening cooperation among Member States.

items.title: DBKL urges responsible lift use after viral clip shows motorcycle inside PPR elevator (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — City Hall (DBKL) has urged residents and delivery riders to treat public housing amenities with care, following a viral video showing an individual riding a motorcycle into a People’s Housing Project (PPR) lift. The closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, which circulated widely across social media, sparked public outrage over safety hazards and property damage. City Hall stressed that functioning elevators are an essential lifeline for public housing (PA) and PPR residents, especially senior citizens, persons with disabilities (OKU), expectant mothers, and young families.

items.title: MTL, super El Nino: Malaysia faces flood and drought risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia faces two weather challenges in the coming months, with heavy rain and floods during the Northeast Monsoon, followed by hotter, drier conditions from a possible Super El Nino that could cause drought, water shortages and affect agriculture. The MTL, which began on Oct 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027, is forecast to bring between three and five episodes of continuous heavy rain, particularly from this November to January next year, thereby increasing the risk of flooding, especially in low-lying areas and near rivers. Flood incidents have also been reported in several states including Perak, Kedah and Negri Sembilan, indicating weather risks that need to be monitored throughout this monsoon season.

items.title: New Chinese ambassador Yao Wen outlines four key priorities to deepen Malaysia-China ties
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 1 — Newly appointed Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Yao Wen has pledged to further strengthen bilateral relations, with greater emphasis on economic cooperation, emerging technologies and people-to-people exchanges. As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship. As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship.

items.title: Palestinian Agriculture Minister: malaysia can build sustainable farming partnerships
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia can turn its continued solidarity with Palestine into a sustainable partnership with Palestinian farmers by cooperating in three key areas to help the agricultural sector recover and enable farmers to earn a living from their land. Palestinian Agriculture Minister Prof Dr Rezq Salimia said the three areas include rehabilitating damaged farms and agricultural infrastructure, strengthening cooperation between academic and agricultural institutions in both countries, and expanding market access for Palestinian products in Malaysia. "Malaysia can turn its concern and solidarity into a sustainable partnership with Palestinian farmers.

items.title: Former AG Idrus Harun among four appointed as members of Judicial Appointments Commission
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appointed four individuals, including former Attorney General Tan Sri Idrus Harun, as members of the Judicial Appointments Commission for a two-year term, effective today. Also appointed are former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali; Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) law lecturer Prof. Dr. Hartini Saripan (for a second term); and former Sabah State Attorney General Datuk Mariati Robert. The Office of the Secretary of the Judicial Appointments Commission, in a statement today, said the appointments were made in accordance with subsection 5(1)(f) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009 [Act 695].

items.title: PM: RM2.5m to provide dialysis facilities at selected Kelantan mosques, plus RM645,000 for water, solar projects
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The government has allocated RM2.5 million to provide dialysis facilities at selected mosques in Kelantan in collaboration with Yayasan Waqaf Malaysia (YWM) and Radicare. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the initiative would improve access to treatment, particularly for rural kidney patients who have to travel long distances to receive dialysis. He said using mosques as dialysis centres would also expand their role in serving local communities.

items.title: EU's new levy on parcels kicks in
items.summary: BRUSSELS, Belgium: The European Union imposed a two-euro (US$2.25) handling fee on packages from outside the 27-nation bloc on Sunday in a bid to curb the influx from China. The handling fee comes on top of the three-euro duty imposed in July on small packages worth less than 150 euros. WHY IS THE EU INTRODUCING THE FEE?

items.title: Avoid 3R provocations, campaign fairly, maturely and with dignity, Azalina tells Melaka poll candidates
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — All candidates, party campaign machinery and supporters of parties contesting the 16th Melaka State Election have been urged to campaign in a fair, mature and dignified manner throughout the 14-day campaign period. Umno Information Chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said also reminded them to comply with election laws and regulations set by the Election Commission (EC), respect differing views and avoid provocations involving sensitivities related to religion, race and the royal institution (3R). Azalina stressed Barisan Nasional’s (BN) position that election campaigns should be centred on candidates’ credentials, service records, manifestos and policy proposals to help voters evaluate their capabilities, experience and vision for Melaka’s future.

items.title: Young candidate Farzana puts livelihoods, infrastructure at heart of Klebang campaign
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan candidate for Klebang, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, 26, is determined to make residents' concerns her top priority if elected. She said several pressing issues in the constituency required attention, including recurring floods, fishermen's jetty infrastructure and efforts to empower housewives and young people economically. "In Klebang, we have padi farmers, fishermen, youths and women.

items.title: Melaka deserves trustworthy, hardworking leaders with integrity, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Melaka deserves trustworthy, hardworking leaders with integrity who are committed to the well-being of its people, said Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that voters in the 16th Melaka state election would choose PH candidates who are committed to bringing meaningful improvements and positive change to the people of the state. Melaka Rumah Kita!

items.title: Canada advancing its 'middle power' strategy with new trade deals, Anand says
items.summary: ATLANTA: Canada is making rapid progress in diversifying its trade and security ties globally, with a goal of doubling its non-US trade over the next decade, Foreign Minister Anita Anand said on Saturday, as Ottawa emphasises trust in building new relationships outside North America. A critic of Lavrov's participation, Anand said the meeting helped illustrate the transformed and fractured nature of the international order, underscoring the need for new approaches, groupings, alliances and partnerships. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed to double Canada's non-US trade over the next decade as President Donald Trump's tariffs have rippled through the Canadian economy.

items.title: China's new ambassador to Malaysia prioritises trade, AI and semiconductors
items.summary: SEPANG: China's newly appointed Ambassador to Malaysia Yao Wen has pledged to further strengthen bilateral relations, with greater emphasis on economic cooperation, emerging technologies and people-to-people exchanges. Yao, 53, arrived from Beijing on Saturday night via an Air China flight, succeeding Ouyang Yujing as China's ambassador to Malaysia. As the first priority, Yao said both countries should strengthen political mutual trust and consolidate their longstanding friendship.

items.title: Anwar prays for Sultan Sharafuddin’s speedy recovery from Influenza A
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has prayed for the recovery of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, who is unwell after contracting Influenza A. “May Allah SWT grant His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah Alhaj Ibni Almarhum Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Alhaj, Sultan and Ruler of Selangor Darul Ehsan, a speedy recovery and good health,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday. Earlier, Istana Alam Shah said in a statement that the infection had been detected by the Sultan’s two personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng, after Sultan Sharafuddin had been experiencing a high fever and weakness in his limbs since the previous morning.

items.title: RM30mil media fund to support digitalisation, safeguard media jobs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Media Innovation Fund 2.0 reflects the government's continued commitment to ensuring the sustainability of local media companies and preventing retrenchments amid industry headwinds. "The Media Innovation Fund is not merely financial assistance for media organisations; it serves as a strategic government investment to secure the future of the nation's journalism industry. Nur-ul Afida also welcomed the introduction of a new funding scope for news service and media content subscriptions, noting it aligned with Bernama's mandate as the national news agency and primary content provider for domestic media outlets.

items.title: Spanish village holds memorial Mass for 69 train crash victims
items.summary: URDA: Residents and local officials gathered on Saturday in a Spanish village near the site of a high-speed train collision that killed at least 69 people for a memorial Mass honouring the victims. The pews inside the San Juan Bautista church in Urda, in the central province of Toledo, were packed, while dozens more people gathered outside to listen to the service. Investigators are looking into the cause of one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville crashed into a stationary train on Wednesday.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia expected to consolidate next week, trade within 1,600-1,630 level
items.summary: On the index board, the FBM Emas Index added 68.28 points to 12,061.73, the FBM Top 100 Index increased 66.25 points to 11,863.86, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index garnered 139.34 points to 12,082.91. The FBM ACE Index rose 57.77 points to 5,403.91, and the FBM Mid 70 Index went up 250.36 points to 17,420.69. Weekly turnover increased to 15.53 billion units worth RM9.97 billion from 14.21 billion units worth RM12.55 billion in the previous week.

items.title: South Korea exports nearly double in October, strongest growth since 1974
items.summary: Exports from Asia's fourth-largest economy, a bellwether for global trade, rose 93.70 per cent last month to US$115.28 billion, slightly higher than the median forecast of a 93.20 per cent increase in a Reuters poll of economists. Imports rose 36.00 per cent to US$72.78 billion, following a 26.00 per cent increase in September, marking the biggest annual rise since January 2022. The country's monthly trade balance recorded a surplus of US$42.50 billion, narrower than the record US$49.97 billion surplus in the previous month.

items.title: Iran warns US, Israel against new attacks after Trump, Netanyahu threats
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's supreme leader warned the United States and Israel Saturday of fresh attacks following their threats to resume strikes after crucial elections, as fears increased over a return to fighting. President Donald Trump suggested he could launch fresh military action after the United States holds its midterm elections early next week. Iran has previously warned it would consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Ringgit expected to trade in narrow range vs greenback ahead of BNM's OPR decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range against the US dollar next week as investors turn their attention to Bank Negara Malaysia's overnight policy rate (OPR) decision on Nov 5. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said a potential OPR hike next week could provide support for the ringgit, as the central bank may consider normalising the policy rate in view of the country's stronger-than-expected economic growth trajectory. "Perhaps, the dollar-ringgit would range between RM4.05 to RM4.07 next week," it said.

items.title: Driver blames Waze after tour bus wedges under bridge with 30 aboard in Butterworth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — A tour bus carrying over 30 passengers from Johor became wedged under a flyover in Taman Bagan of Butterworth, Penang, last night after the driver alleged followed directions from the Waze navigation app. The crash lodged nearly half the bus beneath the low-clearance structure, shattering several windows and showering the road with glass shards. Two passengers suffered minor injuries from flying glass but are reported to be in stable condition, Berita Harian reported.

items.title: Anwar: Islamic education in Kelantan gets continued support with RM9.36m for 23 schools, plus RM6.6m more
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The government will continue to strengthen the development of Islamic education in Kelantan through continuous financial assistance, infrastructure upgrades and the empowerment of traditional educational institutions, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this commitment is being translated into action through various targeted initiatives to ensure that Islamic educational institutions in the state, particularly religious and pondok schools (traditional Islamic religious schools), operate in a conducive learning environment. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government allocated RM9.36 million to 23 Islamic educational institutions in Kelantan in 2025, and approved an additional RM6.628 million this year to support 42 other institutions.

items.title: Govt committed to opening university pathways for ‘pondok’ students, says PM
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Nov 1 — The government is committed to creating opportunities for students of pondok (traditional Islamic religious schools) to pursue higher education up to university level, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Meanwhile, Anwar said pondok institutions served a role beyond religious education, acting as a bastion for safeguarding Islamic faith and strengthening the Muslim community. Earlier, Anwar also presented a RM200,000 contribution to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah.

items.title: Public Service Dept allocates RM1.46m to upgrade village, school
items.summary: GOPENG: THE Public Service Department (PSD) has allocated RM1.465 million for physical improvement and community projects under the Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes. The initiative benefits Kampung Kota Bharu in Kampar and SMK Malim Nawar, with eight of nine planned physical projects completed. The projects include upgrading Masjid Jamek Kota Bharu , the community hall, health clinic, police station and primary school facilities.

items.title: Kerian flood evacuees fall to 18 as situation improves
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 1 — The number of flood victims in the Kerian district has decreased, with 18 individuals from seven families remaining at a relief centre (PPS), down from 25 individuals from nine families yesterday. The victims, all from Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1, have been housed at the centre since last Thursday. Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast thunderstorms this afternoon across all districts, except Kerian, Manjung, and Bagan Datuk.

items.title: Palace: Selangor Sultan contracts Influenza A, investiture ceremony postponed
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 1 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has contracted Influenza A and has been advised to rest for five to seven days to ensure a full recovery. Istana Alam Shah said in a statement yesterday that His Royal Highness’s personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng, detected symptoms of the infection on Friday morning after the Sultan developed a high fever and body weakness. The statement said the Selangor ruler was believed to have contracted the virus while attending public functions and interacting with members of the public, including at outdoor events.

items.title: FBI blames North Korea for US$6.34b Binance crypto heist
items.summary: NEW YORK: The FBI on Saturday accused North Korea of stealing more than US$6 billion in virtual assets from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance in what is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist. The US law enforcement agency's statement came as Binance offered reassurances it was covering the losses from the hacking attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 per cent of what was stolen. Binance is the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes.

items.title: Mother, daughter arrested after stray dog operation scuffle injures Muar council officer
items.summary: MUAR, Nov 1 — Police have arrested a mother and daughter for allegedly obstructing and injuring a female Muar Municipal Council (MPM) enforcement officer during dog-catching operation in Bukit Pasir. The incident occurred at Taman Bintang Emas around 5.55am on Thursday, later triggering public outcry after photos of the injured officer lying on the pavement circulated widely on social media. Muar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the suspects, aged 52 and 24, were detained to facilitate investigations into obstructing a public servant from discharging their duties.

items.title: Myanmar begins releasing Rakhine returnees from Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Myanmar's military authorities have begun releasing ethnic Rakhine nationals repatriated from Malaysia after Kuala Lumpur sought clarification over their reported detention. The Irrawaddy reported that more than 400 ethnic Rakhine were among nearly 1,500 Myanmar nationals repatriated from Malaysia in late September. The programme envisaged returning 5,000 Myanmar nationals in stages.

items.title: #NSTviral: Chinese teen wins praise for graceful Zapin performance
items.summary: Aza Jemima Ahmad KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian Chinese teenager has won praise online for his graceful performance of the traditional Malay dance Zapin. Speaking to the New Straits Times, Eddy said Tan had no professional dance experience before taking up the art in 2025. "The dancers regularly attend Zapin workshops and undergo training at school," Eddy said.

items.title: Judge dismisses Trump's US$10b lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A US judge on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Trump had sued for US$10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the president's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman. The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."

items.title: Smart sharpens flood-rescue skills ahead of northeast monsoon [WATCH]
items.summary: SEPANG: Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) personnel recently honed their flood-rescue skills in a five-day exercise ahead of the northeast monsoon. The Boat Handling and Water Rescue Training programme ran from Oct 19 to 23 at the Pantai Bagan Lalang General Operations Force post. "We are already trained in boat handling, the use of surface rescue equipment and specialised underwater rescue equipment.

items.title: Kota Baru's forgotten flavours take centre stage in Unesco bid
items.summary: For the Kota Baru Gastronomy Club, the mission is to bring the state's rich culinary heritage out of the shadows and into the international spotlight, with the ultimate goal of securing a place on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation's (Unesco) Creative Cities Network. These are among more than 1,000 traditional Kelantanese dishes the club is painstakingly researching and cataloguing as part of its bid to have Kota Baru designated a Unesco Creative City of Gastronomy next year. "We want to highlight Kota Baru and introduce the uniqueness of Kelantanese cuisine to people beyond the state, including the international community," club founder Ariza Mohd Yusoff told the New Straits Times.

items.title: All eyes on Melaka as 79 candidates vie for 28 seats [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: All eyes will be on Melaka over the next 14 days as 79 candidates enter the fray for the 28 seats up for grabs in the state election. One of the surprises was Bersatu's decision to drop out of the Gadek race, despite having earlier announced its candidate for the seat. Barisan Nasional is fielding Melaka MIC deputy chairman S. Nadarajah to defend the seat against three challengers.

items.title: PN's surrender of Melaka seats to MCA weakens BN leverage in Pas states
items.summary: International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst Assoc Prof Dr Syaza Shukri said Perikatan Nasional's surrender of Bandar Hilir and Kota Laksamana to MCA could raise expectations for BN to make reciprocal concessions in Pas-dominated states. In Kedah, he said, Pas' dominance could require BN to concede more. he said, adding that wider negotiations could involve trade-offs between BN and Pas strongholds.

items.title: Flushed, binned, forgotten: How unwanted medicines are putting Malaysia’s waterways at risk (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — From disrupting fish reproduction to altering aquatic behaviour, pharmaceutical residues can have far-reaching effects on ecosystems when expired or unwanted medicines are improperly discarded. As pharmaceutical consumption rises alongside Malaysia’s growing and ageing population, the volume of unwanted medicines requiring proper disposal is also likely to increase. According to the Health Ministry’s Pharmaceutical Services Programme (PSP), many people mistakenly believe expired medicines can be thrown away with household waste, while others bury unused medication under the assumption that it is safer.

items.title: France protests turn violent as 565 arrested, police injured
items.summary: PARIS: Clashes erupted in Paris and other French cities on Saturday after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests at soaring living costs. The interior ministry said late Saturday that police had arrested 565 people across the country. The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles.

items.title: Rioters loot shops as Gen Z protests erupt into violence across Germany
items.summary: FRANKFURT: Masked rioters looted shops in the German city of Frankfurt on Saturday as massive demonstrations turned violent across the country, with police also firing water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined youth-led protests across the country organised by the group "GenZ regelt!" "Violent riots" were taking place, police said in a statement.

items.title: King Charles to address Commonwealth with 'unflinching honesty' amid slavery focus
items.summary: ST. JOHN'S, Antigua and Barbuda: King Charles III will confront "shameful aspects" of UK history with "unflinching honesty" when he addresses Commonwealth leaders next week, Buckingham Palace said Saturday, amid renewed scrutiny of Britain's role in historical transatlantic slavery. The issues have resurfaced as Charles tours the Caribbean before delivering a speech Tuesday at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting there, which Burnham is also set to attend. - SLAVERY PRESSURE - Under pressure from Commonwealth countries over Britain's pivotal part in transatlantic slavery, Burnham penned a newspaper op-ed published earlier Saturday that argued: "We need to face up to the past."

items.title: Fahmi offers condolences to family of Mata Ayer state assemblyman Wan Badariah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer State Assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who passed away today. Fahmi also prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins, bless her soul, and place her among the believers and the righteous. Wan Badariah passed away at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm.

items.title: Anwar directs Education Ministry to act firmly on school bullying
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Education (MOE) to take firm action against bullying in schools amid growing concerns over children’s safety and well-being. He said cases involving children, including suicide, abuse and bullying, highlighted the need to strengthen character development and moral values from an early age. Anwar said academic excellence alone was insufficient, stressing that education must also instil good manners, respect and a sense of responsibility among students.

items.title: Anwar, Lawrence Wong to witness JS-SEZ master plan launch; Perak venue under review, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said it had been agreed that the launch would be witnessed jointly by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart, Lawrence Wong. “Both prime ministers have agreed to witness the launch of the master plan. On preparations for Monday’s bilateral meeting in Singapore, Akmal Nasrullah said Singapore would host the meeting.

items.title: National Courier Day: Govt pledges reform as RM6.9b courier sector takes spotlight
items.summary: MCMC said the government remains committed to strengthening the postal and courier industry through regulatory reform, strategic cooperation and digital transformation to improve service efficiency, industry competitiveness and consumer safety. “On regulatory reform, the government is reviewing proposed amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012 (Act 741) and plans to gazette the Postal Services Regulations (Postal Service Security and Prohibited Postal Articles) 2026 (PSR2026), subject to the relevant approval process. Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali, AMEC chairman Ronald Tan, and representatives of government agencies, postal and courier industry players.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming urges global cooperation on housing crisis, cites 3.4 billion affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Stronger international cooperation is needed to address the global housing crisis, with approximately 3.4 billion people worldwide experiencing some form of inadequate housing, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. The event, themed “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, is jointly organised by UN-Habitat, China’s Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian Provincial People’s Government and the Fuzhou Municipal People’s Government. He highlighted the Malaysia Madani vision, the country’s housing reform agenda, and the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as key initiatives to improve housing accessibility and support sustainable urban development.

items.title: KL police arrest 18 Taiwanese for posing as Hong Kong police in online scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police detained 18 Taiwanese nationals suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate impersonating Hong Kong police after raids on two luxury apartment units here on Thursday. Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said 17 men and one woman, aged between 19 and 43, were arrested during the 6.35pm raid. “Police seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops, and two sets of Hong Kong police uniforms,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar contributes RM200,000 to madrasah in Pondok Lubuk Tapah for repairs
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented a contribution of RM200,000 to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah here. Also present were Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah was founded in 1931.

items.title: RM16b in SARA, STR aid for Malaysians as helping the poor won’t bankrupt the govt, says Anwar
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government will not become poor or go bankrupt by helping the less fortunate, as the real threats to the country’s economy are misconduct among leaders, corruption and financial leakages, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said providing assistance to low-income groups was the government’s responsibility to ensure that the benefits of national development were shared more widely among the people. “No country or government has ever become poor simply by helping the poor,” he said when launching the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.

items.title: Anwar unveils additional RM200m grant to support low-income, small-scale entrepreneurs
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government has allocated an additional grant of about RM200 million to strengthen the capacity of small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly those from low-income groups, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said small-scale financial assistance could generate meaningful returns for traders if channelled to meet their specific business requirements. On the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme, Anwar said more than 4,000 applications had been received from B40 entrepreneurs, with 446 approved so far.

items.title: Anwar: Golok River mouth widening project to cut flood risk, talks with Thailand to wrap up within a month
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Golok River mouth widening project within a month to reduce flood risks in Kelantan and southern Thailand. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had held two rounds of talks with the Thai government, including with his counterpart Anutin Charnvirakul, to expedite the implementation of the project. Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.

items.title: All relief centres closed in Kedah, Negeri Sembilan as floods subside, Perak evacuees fall to 25
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Floods in Kedah and Negeri Sembilan have fully subsided, with all three temporary relief centres (PPS) in the two states closed today, while the number of evacuees in Perak has declined. In Kedah, the last relief centre in Pendang, Dewan Pejabat Penghulu Mukim Bukit Raya, which had been open since last Wednesday, was closed at 10am, allowing all nine evacuees from two families to return home after the floodwaters receded completely. In Negeri Sembilan, two relief centres in Kuala Pilah, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Undang Johol and Dewan Orang Ramai Dangi, which housed 87 evacuees from 35 families, were also closed at 4pm today following improved weather and the complete recession of floodwaters.

items.title: No unhealthy readings: Cheras highest at 77 as 47 areas nationwide record moderate API readings this afternoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A total of 47 areas across the country recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at a moderate level as of this evening, while 21 areas recorded good air quality. In Sarawak, seven areas recorded moderate readings: Mukah (64), IPD Serian (59), Kuching (57), Samalaju (56), Sri Aman (55), Sibu (53), and Samarahan (51). Kedah also recorded moderate readings in Sungai Petani (58) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51), while Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu recorded a reading of 55, and Labuan recorded 52.

items.title: Perlis PAS announces death of Mata Ayer rep Wan Badariah
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 31 — Mata Ayer assemblywoman Wan Badariah Wan Saad died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) here at 4.26pm today. Perlis PAS Information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim announced her death in a post on the Perlis PAS Facebook page. He also extended condolences to her family and urged the public to pray for her soul.

items.title: Baby buried in Kapit still hospitalised; mother’s postpartum depression link unconfirmed, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression. Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother. Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.

items.title: Not compulsory, but journalists, your annual check-up could soon come with your press card
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage. Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.
